react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on pyrimidine metabolism as the dominant disturbed pathway in the treatment group. RaMP multi-database ORA returns KEGG:map00240 (Pyrimidine metabolism), WikiPathways WP4022 (Pyrimidine metabolism), and Reactome R-HSA-73621 (Pyrimidine catabolism) all at FDR 1.74×10⁻¹⁰ with four shared driver metabolites: 2'-deoxyuridine (CHEBI:16450), uridine 5'-monophosphate (CHEBI:16695), 5,6-dihydrouracil (CHEBI:15901), and N-carbamoyl-β-alanine (CHEBI:18261). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently identifies hsa00240 as rank 1 (p=4.47×10⁻⁶) with the identical four compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct networking recovers MUMM:pyrimidine_metabolism as its top hit (p=5.88×10⁻⁴) and additionally flags CDP (CHEBI:17239) and deoxyribose 1-phosphate (CHEBI:11563), which fall below ORA detection thresholds due to their downstream network positions. β-Alanine metabolism (KEGG:map00410 / hsa00410) emerges as a secondary signal, sharing dihydrouracil and ureidopropionic acid with the pyrimidine catabolism axis. Spironolactone (CHEBI:9241, C07310) and methionine sulfoxide (CHEBI:17016, C02989) did not reach significance in any paradigm, suggesting they are treatment-specific pharmacologics or oxidative-stress markers that do not drive the core nucleotide metabolic dysregulation. The convergence across ORA frequency-based, m/z-network, and KEGG-graph paradigms provides high-confidence evidence that the treatment disrupts de novo and catabolic arms of pyrimidine metabolism, with accumulation of dihydrouracil and ureidopropionic acid consistent with a dihydropyrimidinase or ureidopropionase blockade.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on pyrimidine metabolism as the dominant disturbed pathway. RaMP multi-database ORA (FDR 1.74×10⁻¹⁰) returns Pyrimidine metabolism WP:WP4022 as rank 2 and KEGG:map00240 as rank 7, both driven by the same four metabolites: 2'-deoxyuridine (KEGG:C00526), uridine 5'-monophosphate (KEGG:C00105), 5,6-dihydrouracil (KEGG:C00429), and N-carbamoyl-β-alanine (KEGG:C02642). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently identifies KEGG:hsa00240 as rank 1 (p = 4.47×10⁻⁶), hitting the same four compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct networking recovers MUMM:pyrimidine_metabolism as its top hit (p = 9.24×10⁻⁴, overlap 13/14), additionally flagging CDP (KEGG:C00112) and deoxyribose 1-phosphate (KEGG:C00672) that fall below ORA detection thresholds due to downstream network positions. The six shared driver metabolites are canonical pyrimidine catabolism intermediates. Secondary enrichment appears in beta-alanine metabolism (KEGG:hsa00410, rank 3, p = 0.0024; KEGG:map00410, rank 14, FDR 3.17×10⁻⁵), consistent with the ureidopropionic-acid/dihydrouracil branch of the dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase pathway. Spironolactone and methionine sulfoxide are treatment-specific pharmacologics or oxidative-stress markers that do not drive the core nucleotide metabolic dysregulation.

The four driver metabolites shared across both methods are 2'-deoxyuridine, uridine 5'-monophosphate, 5,6-dihydrouracil, and N-carbamoyl-β-alanine, all canonical intermediates of the pyrimidine catabolism branch centred on the dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase step. These four compounds map to the ureidopropionic acid/dihydrouracil branch of pyrimidine degradation and are consistent with the metabolite roster reported by RaMP for REACT:R-HSA-73621 'Pyrimidine catabolism' (rank 1) and WP:WP4022 'Pyrimidine metabolism' (rank 2). The remaining input compounds — CDP, spironolactone, methionine sulfoxide, 1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid, and deoxyribose 1-phosphate — do not appear in the ORA hit list, placing them at downstream network positions beyond the enrichment detection threshold.
